title: Medical Platform Modernization
description: Modernizing a medical document platform from legacy C# and .NET 4.8 to React and .NET 8, including the SSO login flow.
tagline: Giving a legacy medical document platform a modern face and a modern engine.
overview: A medical document management platform for a life-sciences client, moving from a legacy .NET 4.8 stack to React on the front and .NET 8 on the back.
did: Rebuilt legacy C# pages as React frontend pages, turning client requirements into working screens and adapting the backend as those requirements evolved.
Migrated the backend from .NET Framework 4.8 to .NET 8.
Owned the SSO login flow (SAML and OIDC), the most critical path in the platform, and spent a lot of my time debugging and tracing it end to end.
Concentrated on log records and audit logging, so issues can be traced quickly and compliance needs are met.
Built the role-based user management portal (AD and non-AD access), document approval workflows, JWT-based module flows and AWS S3-backed storage.
takeaway: I loved taking real client requirements and watching an old system turn into something new, one page at a time.

title: Legacy Application Modernization
description: Modernizing a 16-year-old application with a focus on responsiveness, data-load speed and real user feedback.
kind: Client project at Minfy Technologies (client details withheld)
tagline: Bringing a 16-year-old application into the modern web.
overview: The client needs a 16-year-old application modernized, with responsiveness and data-load speed as the main goals.
did: Building the frontend as individual, scoped pages, each focused on one clear job.
Designing a dashboard that has to show a large amount of dense, cluttered data in the clearest format possible. It is a genuinely difficult design challenge, and one I enjoy.
Optimizing for responsiveness across screen sizes and for fast data loading.
Speaking directly with real customers, learning their real use cases, and adjusting the design to match their thoughts and processes.
takeaway: Real users beat assumptions every time. The best decisions came from listening to how people actually work.

title: Chotaa Notion - Real-Time Collaboration
description: My internship MVP inspired by Notion, demonstrating real-time collaboration with Socket.IO and WebSockets.
tagline: The project that launched my professional career.
overview: An MVP inspired by Notion, built during my internship to demonstrate Socket.IO and WebSockets keeping multiple live connections in sync.
did: Built collaborative document editing so several people can work in the same document at once.
Used Socket.IO and WebSockets to maintain multiple simultaneous connections.
Built the app on the MERN stack with Firebase and a user-friendly interface for team use.
takeaway: This is the project that took me from learning into a professional career.

title: Budget Planner
description: My first full-stack project: a MERN expense tracker with budget limits, filtering and secure authentication.
tagline: My first full-stack build, and my first real look at how the internet works.
overview: A full-stack expense tracker with budget limits, filtering and secure authentication to help manage personal finances.
did: Explored the whole MERN stack for the first time: MongoDB, Express, React and Node.js.
Added budget limits, expense filtering and JWT-based secure authentication.
Followed how data travels from one point to another, from the browser through the API and database and back.
takeaway: I learned how things on the internet really work, on the MERN development side and on how data moves across the web.

title: Kliks - Photography Portfolio
description: My photography showcase, where my hobbies of photography and nature exploration meet my passion for development.
tagline: Where my love of photography and nature meets my passion for development.
overview: A responsive photography portfolio that showcases my photography and nature-exploration hobbies in a clean, gallery-style experience.
did: Designed and built a responsive, gallery-style experience in React.
Used it as a place to bring my hobbies, photography and exploring nature, together with building for the web.
takeaway: Proof that a hobby and a career can feed each other.
